name: Coral bleaching
summary: No fifth global bleaching event declared as of 16 Nov; El Niño heat raises the risk of one
state: NOAA said in June that the fourth global bleaching event likely ended at the end of 2025, and no fifth event had been declared as of 23 Sep, though scientists warned the El Niño could accelerate mass bleaching (Sierra Club). Searches on 16 Nov found no new global declaration or confirmed regional mass bleaching, so the level stays Normal with an upward trend as El Niño heat builds.
for_you: Mass bleaching would hit reef fisheries, coastal tourism and shoreline protection in tropical countries. Divers and visitors to reefs can check local marine park notices.
rubric_hit: No global bleaching event in progress or confirmed regional mass bleaching: Normal

sources.title: Sierra Club — Corals face an existential threat as the super El Niño heats up

why: Reefs support a quarter of marine species and coastal economies; mass bleaching is a direct sign of ocean heat stress.
drivers: Marine heatwaves, El Niño, warming trend.

rubric.alert: Bleaching extent at record levels with active new alerts in the past month.
rubric.watch: Global bleaching event in progress, or regional mass bleaching.
rubric.normal: No global bleaching event in progress.
